answer: Slashing bonds make a Sybil swarm pay a recurring bill before it earns anything. Each identity must lock a stake while its answers are scored, so ten thousand cloned agents demand ten thousand locked balances and as many costly inference runs. A washed answer, or a fable passed off as proof, triggers slashing; an attacker who lets one node wander off script forfeits that stake. The marginal cost rises per clone while rewards arrive only if real work survives grading, so copying yourself stops being cheap. Payouts sit behind one wharf of verified work.
